newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle to sell unit, hires adviser.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle to sell unit, hires adviser.

text.p: American Eagle Group Inc said its subsidiary, American Eagle Insurance Co, has entered into a letter of intent to sell the artisan contractor line of business of its property and casualty division for an undisclosed amount.

American Eagle also said it has engaged Credit Suisse First Boston to consider alternatives to maximize shareholder value, including the sale of the company, a rights offering, sale of securities, or other options to increase underwriting capacity.
The unit's assets and continuing business will be sold to a newly formed managing general agency controlled by the current executive management of the division.

Chartwell Re Holdings Corp, a unit of Chartwell Re Corp, will hold an equity interest in the managing general agency, and another Chartwell unit, the The Insurance Corp of New York will provide the policy issuing capacity as rates and forms are approved, the company said.
The sale is the final step in the company's strategic plan to withdraw from the specialty property and casualty lines of business, American Eagle said.
American Eagle, which expects to recognize an "immaterial gain" on the transaction, said it would now focus its operations on its core general aviation insurance business.

The company also said it has reached an expanded underwriting agreement with Zurich Reinsurance Centre Holdings Inc to make policies issued by an insurer rated "A" by A.M. Best Co available to American Eagle's aviation insureds.

American Financial Group Inc, which made a $35 million capital investment in the company, has opted to not proceed with the previously announced deal to provide the company's insureds with the security of policies issued by a carrier rated "A" by A.M. Best Co.
Also, Thomas Hayes and Gary Gruber, representatives of American Financial on the American Eagle board, have resigned, the company said.
The company was not immediately available to provide further details.
